question: The HCF and the LCM of two numbers are 5 and 3190, respectively. If one of the numbers is 110, find the other one.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the property of numbers:

Other Number = (HCF × LCM) ÷ First Number

Other Number = (5 × 3190) ÷ 110

Other Number = 15950 ÷ 110 = 145

**∴ The correct answer is 145.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

HCF = 5

LCM = 3190

First number = 110

**Formula Used:**

Product of two numbers = HCF × LCM

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the other number be x.

⇒ First number × Second number = HCF × LCM

⇒ 110 × x = 5 × 3190

⇒ 110 × x = 15950

⇒ x = 15950 ÷ 110

⇒ x = 1595 ÷ 11

⇒ x = 145

**∴ The correct answer is 145.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Rule for HCF and LCM

For any two numbers a and b, the product of the numbers is always equal to the product of their HCF and LCM (a × b = HCF × LCM).

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are considered co-prime if their Highest Common Factor (HCF) is 1. In this case, their Least Common Multiple (LCM) is exactly the product of the two numbers.

HCF and LCM of Fractions

HCF = (HCF of Numerators) ÷ (LCM of Denominators) 
 LCM = (LCM of Numerators) ÷ (HCF of Denominators)
